record.paper_title: On Some Open Problems of Mahmoudi and Renshaw
record.context_brief: Cyclic acts over infinite inverse semigroups
record.original_question: If S is an infinite inverse semigroup, must every cyclic right S-act S/ρ admit a (P)-cover? Here an inverse semigroup is a semigroup that is regular and whose idempotents commute, a cyclic right S-act is an act generated by one element, and a (P)-cover is a cover by an act satisfying condition (P).

evidence.quote: In [9] the author also posed the open problem: Do infinite inverse semigroups have the property that all cyclic S-acts have a (P)-cover? (The open problem 2 in [9].) In the following we will consider this problem.
Theorem 2.21. Let S be an infinite inverse monoid. If all left unitary submonoids of S are right unitary, then all cyclic S-acts have a (P)-cover.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be an inverse semigroup, that is, a semigroup in which every element $a$ has a unique inverse $a^{-1}$ satisfying $a a^{-1} a = a$ and $a^{-1} a a^{-1} = a^{-1}$, and in which all idempotents commute. A right $S$-act is a set $A$ equipped with a right action $A \times S \to A$, $(a,s) \mapsto as$, satisfying $(as)t = a(st)$. A right $S$-act is called cyclic if it is generated by a single element; equivalently, it is isomorphic to a quotient $S/\rho$ of $S$ (with $S^1$ acting on the right) by a right congruence $\rho$. A right $S$-act $B$ is said to satisfy condition (P) if whenever $bs = b's'$ in $B$ for $b,b' \in B$ and $s,s' \in S$, there exist $c \in B$ and $u,v \in S$ with $b = cu$, $b' = cv$ and $us = vs'$. A (P)-cover of a right $S$-act $A$ is a surjective $S$-homomorphism $f \colon B \to A$ where $B$ satisfies condition (P) and such that $f$ has no proper "essential" subact mapping onto $A$ (i.e. if $g \colon C \to B$ is an $S$-homomorphism with $C$ satisfying (P) and $f \circ g$ surjective, then $g$ is surjective).

Question: If $S$ is an infinite inverse semigroup, must every cyclic right $S$-act $S/\rho$ admit a (P)-cover?
artifact.status_search_result: The question originates as one of the open problems posed by Mahmoudi and Renshaw (2008) on covers of cyclic acts over monoids. Partial results are known: under additional hypotheses (e.g. for an infinite inverse monoid in which every left unitary submonoid is also right unitary) all cyclic acts admit a (P)-cover. The general question for arbitrary infinite inverse semigroups does not appear to have a complete published resolution; related uniqueness questions for strongly flat covers were also reported as still open in subsequent work.

status_evidence.title: On covers of cyclic acts over monoids
status_evidence.snippet: Mahmoudi and Renshaw define a strongly flat cover ((P)-cover) and give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of such covers.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of (P)-cover and its existence problem were introduced by Mahmoudi and Renshaw, who posed open problems including the one for infinite inverse semigroups.

status_evidence.title: Covers of acts over monoids and pure epimorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Mahmoudi and Renshaw ... left open a number of questions regarding the 'other' definition. Two recent papers have suggested ... however, these examples are in fact false and so the question ... appears to still remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Several questions raised by Mahmoudi and Renshaw concerning (P)-covers remain open.
